requirements.quote: The long header contains two connection IDs: the Destination Connection ID is chosen by the recipient of the packet and is used to provide consistent routing; the Source Connection ID is used to set the Destination Connection ID used by the peer.
requirements.condition: When constructing or processing a long-header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The long header contains a Destination Connection ID chosen by the packet recipient and a Source Connection ID used to establish the peer's Destination Connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet construction and parsing can verify the presence and roles of both connection ID fields.

requirements.quote: Each endpoint uses the Source Connection ID field to specify the connection ID that is used in the Destination Connection ID field of packets being sent to them.
requirements.condition: During the handshake when an endpoint sends a long-header packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint uses its Source Connection ID field to communicate the connection ID that its peer uses as the Destination Connection ID when sending packets to it.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake packet traces can correlate an endpoint's advertised Source Connection ID with the peer's later Destination Connection ID.

requirements.quote: After processing the first Initial packet, each endpoint sets the Destination Connection ID field in subsequent packets it sends to the value of the Source Connection ID field that it received.
requirements.condition: After an endpoint processes the first Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint sets the Destination Connection ID in subsequent sent packets to the Source Connection ID received in that Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet trace can compare the first received Initial packet's Source Connection ID with subsequent transmitted Destination Connection IDs.

requirements.quote: When an Initial packet is sent by a client that has not previously received an Initial or Retry packet from the server, the client populates the Destination Connection ID field with an unpredictable value.
requirements.condition: When a client sends an Initial packet before receiving any Initial or Retry packet from the server.
requirements.required_behavior: The client populates the Destination Connection ID with an unpredictable value.
requirements.why_checkable: Client Initial generation can be tested or statically inspected to determine whether the initial Destination Connection ID comes from an unpredictability-preserving generation mechanism.

requirements.quote: This Destination Connection ID MUST be at least 8 bytes in length.
requirements.condition: When a client sends an Initial packet before receiving any Initial or Retry packet from the server.
requirements.required_behavior: The Destination Connection ID is at least 8 bytes long.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client uses a Destination Connection ID shorter than 8 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Destination Connection ID length is directly measurable.

requirements.quote: Until a packet is received from the server, the client MUST use the same Destination Connection ID value on all packets in this connection.
requirements.condition: Before the client receives any packet from the server.
requirements.required_behavior: The client uses the same Destination Connection ID value on every packet in the connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client changes the Destination Connection ID before receiving a server packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Successive client packets before the first server packet can be compared for Destination Connection ID equality.

requirements.quote: The Destination Connection ID field from the first Initial packet sent by a client is used to determine packet protection keys for Initial packets.
requirements.condition: When determining packet protection keys for Initial packets.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation uses the Destination Connection ID from the client's first Initial packet as the input that determines the Initial packet protection keys.
requirements.why_checkable: Key-derivation inputs can be instrumented or inspected and compared with the first client Initial packet's Destination Connection ID.

requirements.quote: These keys change after receiving a Retry packet;
requirements.condition: After a Retry packet is received.
requirements.required_behavior: The Initial packet protection keys change.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation continues using the unchanged pre-Retry Initial packet protection keys.
requirements.why_checkable: The Initial protection keys or their derivation inputs before and after Retry processing can be compared.

requirements.quote: The client populates the Source Connection ID field with a value of its choosing
requirements.condition: When the client constructs the relevant handshake packet.
requirements.required_behavior: The client populates the Source Connection ID field with a client-chosen value.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet construction can verify that the client supplies a Source Connection ID value selected by its own connection-ID logic.

requirements.quote: sets the Source Connection ID Length field to indicate the length.
requirements.condition: When the client populates the Source Connection ID field.
requirements.required_behavior: The client sets the Source Connection ID Length field to the actual length of the Source Connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The encoded Source Connection ID Length disagrees with the Source Connection ID's length.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded length field can be compared directly with the number of bytes in the Source Connection ID.

requirements.quote: 0-RTT packets in the first flight use the same Destination Connection ID and Source Connection ID values as the client's first Initial packet.
requirements.condition: When the client sends 0-RTT packets in its first flight.
requirements.required_behavior: Each such 0-RTT packet uses both the Destination Connection ID and Source Connection ID values from the client's first Initial packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A first-flight 0-RTT packet uses a different Destination Connection ID or Source Connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The two connection ID fields in first-flight 0-RTT packets can be compared with those in the client's first Initial packet.

requirements.quote: Upon first receiving an Initial or Retry packet from the server, the client uses the Source Connection ID supplied by the server as the Destination Connection ID for subsequent packets, including any 0-RTT packets.
requirements.condition: Upon the client's first receipt of an Initial or Retry packet from the server.
requirements.required_behavior: The client uses the server-supplied Source Connection ID as the Destination Connection ID in subsequent packets, including subsequent 0-RTT packets.
requirements.why_checkable: The received server Source Connection ID can be compared with the Destination Connection ID in later client packets.

requirements.quote: Once a client has received a valid Initial packet from the server, it MUST discard any subsequent packet it receives on that connection with a different Source Connection ID.
requirements.condition: After a client has received a valid Initial packet from the server, when it receives a later packet on that connection whose Source Connection ID differs.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client accepts or processes the later packet as a valid packet on the connection.
requirements.error_behavior: The client discards the later packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A focused test can send a valid server Initial followed by a packet carrying a different Source Connection ID and observe whether it is discarded.

requirements.quote: A client MUST change the Destination Connection ID it uses for sending packets in response to only the first received Initial or Retry packet.
requirements.condition: When the client receives Initial or Retry packets during connection establishment.
requirements.required_behavior: The client changes its sending Destination Connection ID in response only to the first received Initial or Retry packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client changes its sending Destination Connection ID in response to a later Initial or Retry packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence containing multiple Initial or Retry packets can verify which receipt triggers a Destination Connection ID change.

requirements.quote: A server MUST set the Destination Connection ID it uses for sending packets based on the first received Initial packet.
requirements.condition: When a server receives the first client Initial packet and selects its sending Destination Connection ID.
requirements.required_behavior: The server bases its sending Destination Connection ID on the first received Initial packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server bases the initial selection on a later Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: The first client's Initial packet and the server's subsequent packet headers can be correlated in a packet trace.

requirements.quote: Any further changes to the Destination Connection ID are only permitted if the values are taken from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames;
requirements.condition: After the initial Destination Connection ID selection or permitted first handshake-triggered change, when an endpoint changes its Destination Connection ID again.
requirements.required_behavior: Every further Destination Connection ID value is taken from a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: An endpoint makes a further Destination Connection ID change to a value not obtained from a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection-ID state transitions can be traced to previously received NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame values.

requirements.quote: if subsequent Initial packets include a different Source Connection ID, they MUST be discarded.
requirements.condition: When an Initial packet after the first includes a Source Connection ID different from the established Source Connection ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint accepts or processes that subsequent Initial packet as valid for the connection.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint discards the subsequent Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject a later Initial packet with a different Source Connection ID and observe whether it is discarded.
